review_text: Firts, this is a good product.  I don't want to say they are a poor product, but I want to caution people depending on their needs.  My masks were not being held tight enough to my face, so I got these to hopefully tighten them.  They work as advertised in terms of how they function, and I'm sure that there are a lot of people who it would work for.  The mechanism for attaching them to the ear loops is much better than I thought.  The little "button" that slides into the loop is attached to fabric, not a rigid material.  The result is that there is no problem attaching them to most any thickness of ear loop material.  However,for me, it was too long.  I adapted them to work by looping it around on ear loop and attaching it to the other ear loop, essentially cutting it in half.  It is adjustable, but the shortest length is still 5 1/2 inches long, which I may have missed in the description.  That is way too long for my purposes.  I think part of the reason is that my ear loops are elastic, and when stretched far enough, the distance between them is much shorter.  My advice, measure the distance between the loops when you pull them back far enough for you.  Elastic loops may give more than you think.

product_description: Accepted by leading authorities as a simple and accurate method for discovering congenital color blindness and red-green blindness, each in two forms, complete and incomplete. Includes four special plates for tests to determine the kind and degree of defect in color vision. Makes use of the peculiarity that in red-green blindness, blue and yellow appear remarkably bright compared with red and green. Color plates encased in specially designed album-type books for ease of handling. Detailed instructions included. What is colorblindness? Color blindness (color vision deficiency) is a condition in which certain colors cannot be distinguished, and is most commonly due to an inherited condition. Red/Green color blindness is by far the most common (99%) form and causes problems in distinguishing reds and greens. Another color deficiency Blue/Yellow also exists, but is rare (1%) and there is no commonly available test for it. There is no treatment for color blindness, nor is it usually the cause of any significant disability. However, it can be very frustrating for individuals affected by it. Those who are not color blind seem to have the misconception that color blindness means that a color blind person sees only in black and white or shades of gray. While this sort of condition is possible, it is extremely rare. The Ishihara color test is a test for color blindness. It was named after its designer, Dr. Shinobu Ishihara (1879-1963), a professor at the University of Tokyo, who first published his tests in 1917. It makes use of the peculiarity that in red-green blindness, blue and yellow appear remarkably bright compared to red and green. It consists of a number of colored plates, on each plate is printed a circle made of many different sized dots of slightly different colors, spread in a random manner. Within the dot pattern, and differentiated only by color, is a number. What, or even if, a number is visible indicates if and what form of color blindness the viewer has. The full test consists of thirty-eight plates, but the existence of a deficiency is usually clear after fewer plates. The Ishihara Color Charts are accepted by leading authorities worldwide as a simple and accurate test method. The color plates are available in an album-type book for ease of handling. The books are printed in Japan and are protected by international copyright. Graham-Field has been the exclusive North American wholesale distributor of Ishihara Tests for over 30 years. Published by Kanehara Trading Inc. Tokyo Japan UOM

I was pleased to see that I could get the auger from Amazon Prime without having to but the entire ice maker assembly. Thanks, GE.

I picked the first one on the list, by AppliancePartsPros which was 10 minutes long. The front of the ice maker didn't match the one in our refrigerator, but the insides were the same, so the video was very helpful. Watched it all the way through, and then it took me about 1/2 hour to replace the auger. I would not have wanted to attempt the repair without viewing the video first.

Afterwards, both my wife and I were both amazed at how well the ice maker was working again.

product_description: Installation Instructions: 1) Level the WASHER by rotating front feet with an adjustable wrench to raise/lower. Stick the foam strip along the bottom edge of the DRYER covering small ribs along the bottom edge of the cabinet. Repeat on each edge of the bottom of the DRYER (all four bottom directions). NOTE: Foam strips should not stick out past the edge of DRYER cabinet. 6) With an assistant, lift DRYER on top of WASHER. Line up back of DRYER with back of WASHER. 7) Locate the two horizontal slots in back of DRYER cabinet (directly above stacking bracket screw holes in back of WASHER cabinet). Insert curved end of the metal stacking bracket into horizontal slots on back of DRYER. Attach brackets to the back of the WASHER with provided screws.

product_title: Make your replacement wicks last longer.
review_text: Because of the calcium in local water the wick loses its ability to absorb water over time, as has been noted by many reviewers. The only choice is to throw the wick out or to wash the calcium solids out of the wick and then reuse it. Unfortunately the wick loses its rigidity with the washing and becomes floppy. I discovered that with my humidifier I could wrap the old washed wick around the outside of a new wick, with the new wick providing stability. If needed, paper clips unfolded in the shape of an upside down U can be used to hold the two wicks together, although this has not been necessary for me. The force of the fan pulling in air holds the two wicks together. The two wicks draw up considerably more water and the humidifier is more efficient - and the wicks last much longer. Try it.

product_title: An extremely poorly designed range hood.
product_description: Cosmo presents a modern professional top vented under cabinet range hood that adds bold, distinct flair to your kitchen. Fits easily into an existing cabinet, and has premium brushed stainless steel that matches seamlessly with existing kitchen appliances for a modern upscale look. Our under cabinet range hood features 500 CFM motors with premium stainless steel baffle filters to trap grease and oil. Newly designed, this under cabinet range hood is both energy-saving and quiet, utilizing high lumen LED lighting for year-round cost savings. Our filters save you money year after year and are dishwasher-safe for added convenience. Trust Cosmo for your next kitchen appliance for premium quality at factory-direct prices.
review_text:
I purchased this range hood to go over a range that has an overhanging cabinet. There was no duct to connect it to so I took advantage of the ductless feature. For installation, two strong men and one other person are required to install this extremely heavy range hood. Also, the cabinet that the hood needs to fit under has to have a hole cut into it to allow attachment of the connection point that the duct would connect to if one were present. So that means loss of the storage space where that hole is cut, and a baffle to be installed to keep stored items from falling into the fan blades. As far as performance, other than the lights it worked OK. My wife hates it because she bumps her head against it when cooking.
About 2 months after installing the hood the two LED lights burned out. Without lights it is very dark under the hood. Cosmo sent two replacement lights. The instructions for replacing the lights were for an older model. I had to figure out how to remove and replace the lights, and I was able to figure it out partially. It is only possible to get one hand under the hood position to disconnect and reconnect the lights. If the wires were long enough to insert them and connect them before actually mounting them it would have been doable. But it was impossible. And the sharp metal edges cause abrasions on the wrists.
By the time I had reached the conclusion that the hood was not going to work for me, it was too late to send it back for a refund. So I am out the whole $340 for this unit. I will probably trash or recycle it. Also, it is not easy to find a range hood for my situation, and now I need to find one that is built well and works for my situation. Not an easy task. No I don't recommend Cosmo range hoods! A lot of what they say in the manual is for older models and not applicable to what is actually delivered. They are very heavy. Maybe that's good for some, but installation is a horror story.

product_description: Be prepared for any party or gathering, planned or spur-of-the-moment; with this top selling Compact Ice Maker. This Black ice maker is perfect for outdoor activities and entertaining. The portable design lets you enjoy a cold, refreshing drink anywhere you go. Featuring two cube sizes so you can customize your ice to your drink; and a 2.3 quart reservoir so you can make plenty of ice ahead of time to have on hand. Electronic controls with an LED indicator means you can put in your ice order with the touch of a button and be ready to serve soda, lemonade, cocktails and more. Produces 26 pounds of ice in 24 hours.
review_text:
As I've only had this ice maker two weeks, I cannot attest to it's longevity, but I'll update this review if it doesn't last as long as I think it should.

I first heard of these a few years ago and my skeptical button was immediately pushed. Countertop ice maker. Pshaw!. Then the prices began to come down, and I really wanted to have ice at work without having to haul it from home every day or two. My kids gave me Amazon gift cards for Christmas and my birthday and I just decided - after reading a hundred reviews of several models - to purchase this ice maker.

Still skeptical, but hopeful, (and confident in Amazon if it didn't work) I unpacked the beautiful appliance and set it up. Really the set up consisted of removing the packing tape that held the basket in place and plugging it in. I did rinse the basket out. I poured cold water in the reservoir and in minutes, literally less than 10 minutes the first ice cubes tumbled into the basket. I had meant to throw out the first few ice cubes but couldn't resist popping one in my mouth. If you are an ice eater/chewer (that sounds pretty disgusting actually) you will love this ice. At least with my water (filtered) the ice is white and soft. Not crystalline. And faster than you can imagine, you've got a basket full of ice. I dumped it on a cookie sheet which I put in the freezer (spreading the cubes out a little bit) and then dumped them into a basket in the freezer.

You don't have to do this. you can serve from the basket. But I like lots and lots of ice, so I wanted a bucket of it in the freezer. The cabinet of the icemaker is not refrigerated, so the ice will begin to melt as soon as it is made. For some people this will be a negative; it doesn't matter to me because I want to freeze it anyway. (I don't dump it into to basket in the freezer immediately because it is wet ice and it will freeze into a huge lump instead of individual cubes.)

The machine looks like a bread machine, but a little taller. It's a beautiful red color, kind of new car metal flake color. It's quiet. You hear the water trickle into the "ice tray" and then hear the ice cubes fall into the basket. I have it in my office and it doesn't bother me or clients a bit. When the reservoir runs dry, it stops making ice and a light comes on to let you know to refill the water if you want more ice. If you turn it off with ice in the basket, it simply melts back into the reservoir to be reincarnated into ice the next time you use is.

So far I couldn't be happier. I love having ice - especially this kind of ice - at my office.

I did try out the new filter for a month.
It does work although you’ll need to prepare the aero press while it’s inverted. Hey, it all works which is great.
If you’re familiar with the taste of coffee oils (which mostly get filtered out by paper filters) and you do not like that taste, I do not recommend this product.
If you do not have an issue with this then this product is great and will work as a reusable filer that is easy to clean.
The pressure used to press the coffee into your cup is really weak with this filter as well. The pressure doesn’t get as strong as with paper filters. It still works but takes getting used to.

product_description: ECOFLOW 298Wh Plug-in Battery for GLACIER Portable Refrigerator Up to 40 Hr Runtime, Lithium Battery USB-C 100W Charger for Laptops [GLACIER NOT INCLUDED]
review_text:
March 14, 2022 - After watching Will Prowse's two YouTube videos about the EcoFlow 600 (i.e., the River), both videos made about a year ago, I decided to buy 3 of them and three of the River Extra Batteries to go with them. However, just in case I discovered a problem, I initially ordered one River and one extra battery. It was good that I did because when I added the extra battery to the River it failed miserably.

I had the same problems that Prowse encountered and he solved (to some degree) by a firmware update which was done via the EcoFlow App which he had downloaded to his phone. He had difficulty with the EcoFlow App in making that update, it took hours, but eventually he succeeded.

I never crossed my mind that EcoFlow, knowing that a firmware update was necessary in order for the River to function properly with its extra battery, would send the River out without the update and, thus, in a defective condition. That would leave all of its buyers with a headache to have to deal with immediately after installation of the extra battery. Pretty inconsiderate thing for EoFlow to do.

Here is what happened to me. I received the River and it seemed to work properly. I did not check to DC input (e.g., solar panel input) to verify its maximums as I figured it would be best to do that after I had received and installed the extra battery. I downloaded the EcoFlow app onto an Android phone using version 7.1.2. The app didn’t work. It recognized the River but would not connect to the internet which it had to do in order to effect any upgrade / update to the River. I viewed various YouTube videos on how to make such a connection but they were out-of-date. Nothing I tried worked.

So the next morning, as soon as EcoFlow’ Customer Support Line was available (9am Eastern), I called. However, they were late manning their stations so I go a voice mail prompt. I did as it asked… left my name, my email address and my telephone number.

The battery arrived a few days thereafter. I installed it and charged it up. Next I turned on the inverter, which had worked properly beforehand (as far as providing me with the UPS function, and that is when the problems began. The row of LED lights turned red and the River turned off the inverter. I went through a series of repeated tests, unplugging and replugging, turning the River off and then back on, and more but nothing helped. It was the same problem Prowse had encountered… the UPS function (power flow-through) would not work with the added extra battery. And there was no way I could update the firmware because the EcoFlow app did not work either.

To make matters worse, the River would not recharge. After all of my testing the charge had dropped to 95% and it would not recharge. I used the River until the charge dropped to 92% but, still, it would not recharge. Again a series of tests but it simply would not recharge.

It had been 5 days since I initially called EcoFlow and no one had contacted me. Again, I attempted to reach them by phone and this time I got a nice lady who asked me a series of questions in, what appeared to be, an attempt to diagnosis the problem. However, unless she had just begun to work at EcoFlow, she should have already known what the problem was. Prowse had informed them of it a year ago. Namely, the UPS function did not work with the added battery. She should have acknowledged an awareness of the problem and had a solution ready for me. She did not. So I ended the call before wasting any more time.

I then separated the extra battery from the River and guess what. The River still would not recharge. Everything went back into its original boxes, I made a video tape to prove that all parts were being returned, then sent everything back to Amazon for a full refund.

Conclusion: As I have already stated, there is evidence that EcoFLow is aware of the UPS problem and yet, apparently, they sold these devices in that defective condition anyway. They also know about the problem with their app (Version 2.7.0, Requires Android 5.0 and up) as it is complained about in many places (see the 2.0 rating out of 5.0 at Google Play). Consequently, because I smell unethical individuals at the top of the EcoFlow heap, I will not have any future dealings with them and suggest that others consider doing the same.

review_text:
This has a classic range hood design that can fit almost any kitchen style. The 4 star review is due to the bright light from the buttons and a warranty claim that I had to file. The buttons are back light by a VERY bright blue LED. The LED's are so bright that they dominate the soft glow from the halogen. When I set the halogen lights to their dimmest setting (to create a nice ambiance) the harsh blue LED's completely contrast and kill the mood. I struggle to understand why the LED's and LCD even turn on when using the halogen lights...? I actually corrected this issue by disassembling the keypad/LCD control module and spray painting the underside of the buttons black to block the LED light from shinning through (this worked great!).
The second issue was again with the keypad/LCD control module. The buttons are awkward to push and because of that the mount that holds the module in place broke (it is plastic). So, I had to file a warranty claim with the manufacturer to get a replacement module which I had to install myself (easy, but I did have to pay shipping). To prevent the issue from happening again, I placed some washers behind the module for reinforcement. This helps prevent it from sliding backward when the buttons are pressed (I highly suggest this from the get go).
Overall, this range hood was great for the money. Install was straight forward and it looks great. It is quiet on its lowest setting and you can feel the suction within the room when it is on full suction. I would not hesitate to buy/suggest this to anyone.

I have a Breville Oracle Touch espresso machine with a 58 mm portafilter. I recently purchased a stainless screen for it, since those are becoming popular now, and it worked ok. Because of that, you don't have to make any adjustments to the depth of the brew head. They also are disposable, so there is no cleaning of the filter. There is no residue to speak of on the brew head, so nothing to clean.

I also like that they are unbleached, as they add nothing to the espresso, flavor-wise, and fewer chemicals to deal with. The quality is solid. The design is solid, as well; I like the size and placement of the one hole at the bottom. The No. 4 filters I bought from Amazon (Melitta Cone Coffee Filters, Natural Brown, No. 4) fit very well and make a good team for my morning coffee. I also use the Bodum Bistro Electric Burr Coffee Grinder which I highly recommend.

After having made about half a dozen or so cups I finally got down a system that works for me. Keep in mind that I like my coffee rich and strong. I grind the beans to the finest setting and place them in the filter (which, of course, needs to be placed in the ceramic holder). I put the holder over an empty cup. I then splash some cold or room temperature water on the grounds and filter in order to dampen them. The cup below catches the water. I take the water that has been captured and repeat the process a few times until the grounds and filter are sufficiently damp. This is very important as it causes the boiling water you are about to pour over the grounds to steep longer. An already semi-saturated set of grounds and filter makes a stronger brew.

Meanwhile, I've had a cup of water in the microwave going until it is boiling, boiling, boiling. Once the water is dancing well I simply pour it over the saturated filter and grounds and wait about 30 seconds until my perfect cup is ready. When I want it extra rich I'll even pour the coffee back over the grounds for a second run.

This process is simpler and quicker than it may sound and definitely worth the small effort. The water never touches plastic and the cup is PERFECTO! There is no comparison to a cup of coffee made from an automatic maker (water boiled in plastic - ulgh). I actually like many of the K-cup coffees that I've had, but I like the flavor, and freshness of this process even better (not to mention staying away from water boiled in plastic).

product_description: You’re familiar with “the good ice. ” Those soft, yet crunchy nuggets - almost like tiny snowballs that float in your favorite beverage. It’s the only ice that’s ever excited anyone enough to shout across a crowded room, “They have the good ice here! ” Finally, you can have the good ice anytime you want it, with the GE Profile Opal Nugget Ice Maker. review_text:
I'm taking the effort to tell you my story in the hopes that you don't get deceived by all the positive comments like I did.

I got one of these GE Profile Opal units with a side tank last year. I love the nugget ice you get at fast food/convenience stores and was excited to have my own ice maker at home.

It was great for the first few months but then the misery started.

After about 4 months, this unit started making such a loud squeaking sound that I had to turn it off after 1 hour of operation. I contacted GE Support and they made me to go through ridiculous rounds of emailing pictures, recording videos of the loud sound and several back-forth steps of troubleshooting.

GE finally agreed to replace the unit at no charge but I had to ship the original to them first. What a hassle, took almost 2 months to get through the process and receive the replacement unit.

The replacement unit was clearly refurbished, not new, but it worked. Everything was OK for a year, but then it just suddenly stopped working. I ran it through several rounds of cleaning but nothing worked. I was pretty good at keeping it clean and descaled so I was surprised by the problem.

The unit would start up after I pushed the main button and 5 minutes later it would flash the blue light and turn off. The water bin was full and I could see and hear the water flowing from the top trough…why was the blue light flashing?!

UGH, not again!!

I contacted GE Support, dreading what I knew was coming next.

As expected, they took me through the same ridiculous rounds of troubleshooting as before with the original. After about a week of back-forth emails and phone calls, they finally agreed something was wrong with the unit and it needed to be repaired.

But here's where they get you...GE agreed to repair the unit but they wanted me to pay $250 to cover the shipping because it was technically out of the 1yr warranty.

I said that was unfair, this unit is clearly defective with cheap parts. I bought it because it was supposed to be top quality, so why did it breakdown only after a year of usage.

The GE support rep said he would escalate the issue to his manager and asked me to respond back to his email asking the situation to be reviewed. I sent the email as requested.

After a few days, the manager replied back. His email was a standard copy/paste response and basically said too bad, it's out of warranty, pay up.

I'm extremely dissatisfied with this thing and GE’s support service. I already pumped money and many hours of troubleshooting …no way I'm going to be tricked into putting more money and time into another one.

Based on my direct experience...I believe this model may be designed to breakdown, using poor quality parts that can fail after a year to make more money on the service repairs.

Bottomline, don't be fooled into buying this unit or believing the positive comments. I'm eagerly waiting for others to stand up and file a class action lawsuit.

product_title: Decent machine, but couldn't find a hose that works
review_text:
I'm not sure how to rate this. I use this machine, and it is great for washing about half a laundry-basket-worth of laundry and getting as much water out of the clothes as possible. However, I wish I had never even bothered to try to use or replace the hose and manually filled it with water from the start.

I tried the white intake hose it came with. I got a sink adapter that fit both my sink and the hose perfectly. But the hose leaks between the little plastic part that connects to my adapter and the rubbery hose part. Nearly half the water spewed out. I started only turning the faucet on when the machine made the low buzz indicating it needed to fill. Then, to further save water, I started catching the water and manually filling the machine with the water I caught.

I got a replacement washing machine hose like some of the other reviews mentioned. That hose leaked where it connected to the machine. I contacted the seller. The seller sent me a replacement hose. That hose worked exactly like the original hose, which is to say barely usable. The seller gave me an $18 refund to get my own hose.

I went back to the Home Depot and got a green garden hose plus a $1 tape thing the workers said I could use to redo the different adapters if needed.

The green garden hose doesn't work either. NONE OF IT WORKS.

I took off the inlet hose entirely and moved the machine to my bathroom. I fill it with water from the tub (I'm using a giant cooking pot but will get a bucket on my 4th trip to Home Depot now--have I mentioned I don't actually live anywhere near a Home Depot?). The outtake hose easily and safely goes into my tub, unlike trying to snake it through my dish rack in order to use the machine in my kitchen. Yes, it's a pain to bend over to fill the pot, but it absolutely beats trying to use this with an intake hose. Also, it is a lot less ugly in the middle of one of my rooms without a bunch of ungainly hoses and sink adapters connected to it.

My advice if you're not super hardware-handy and want to use this machine:
Put it in your bathroom. Unless you have an exceptionally low sink, you need the low-ness of a tub or shower floor to use the outtake hose (gray hose the water goes out of) easily.

Don't bother with the intake (white) hose! Try out a replacement if you happen to have one, but neither a washing machine hose or the "green garden hose" everyone keeps saying works worked for me, and that was on top of getting an adapter for my sink and special tape. Just manually fill the machine with water. I'd say it needs maybe 4 gallons to start and 4 more throughout the wash (it will stop agitating and make a low buzzing sound that will alert you when to add more water). I like manually filling because it allows me to control the temp of the water, goes faster, and is one less hose coming out of the machine.

Other things I would have liked to know before purchasing:
It's actually quite large and heavy. I find it easy to move by "walking" it, definitely not lifting it. The reason I bring it up is because this machine seems to me most practical for people in small city apartments, and so many things about it are not suited for . . . small city apartments. When I had it in my kitchen, with all the hoses attached, it was a giant eye sore that pissed me off every time I saw it.
With about 13 minutes to go in the low water cycle, it starts slamming around and making a TON of noise. Again, super not suitable if you live above someone.
The shortest possible full cycle is still 37 minutes. I was hoping it would be more customizable. On regular machines you can have a "quick wash" for no more than 25 minutes.

I have no idea if I would repurchase this. It's a super large, heavy appliance, which I'm not fond of in general. I hope to one day have in-unit laundry (a girl can dreeeeeeeam), so I already wonder how to move this thing and how I would get rid of it if needed. Unlike a normal washing machine, there might be other set-ups where this machine doesn't work, such as a place with in-unit or a nice, cheap-ish laundry room. It also gets very loud and smashes against the ground in the soak cycle. This is totally fine in my mom's first floor laundry room in her house, for example, but on the top floor of an apartment building where my landlord probably doesn't want me to even have an after-market water-filled device, it's a little nerve-wracking. It was super frustrating to mess around with the intake hose and try to figure it out, making multiple hardware store trips, talking to all sorts of people for solutions, etc. In the back of my head I still want to just call a Task Rabbit out, lay out all my hoses and adapter, and see if someone can figure it out.

Also, it was $170! For me, that's a lot of money for something with an integral piece that doesn't work for anyone out of the box. I have a laundry room in my building, but it's $2.75 for a wash and $2.50 for a dry, so I hoped this would be more convenient and cheaper in the long run. Convenient . . . I'm not sure. It's in my place and never being used by someone else, so that's nice, but the manual water filling and worrying about it isn't great. It also obviously doesn't dry the clothes, not that it advertises to do so, so convenience-wise if you have an alternative like on-site laundry or a laundromat I don't know if this is actually more convenient. Price-wise, again, I'm skipping the drying entirely, so obviously this is going to work out to be cheaper. I've used it probably more than a dozen times now, so it's saved me spending more money in the laundry room but definitely isn't anywhere close to paying for itself yet.

I recommend it if you're familiar with portable washers and know it will work for you and your space. If you're used to stuff-and-don't-worry-about-it washers and towels fluffy from the dryer, I don't think this machine is worth the price and hassle.
